name: Manish Sood
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Reltio (sources differ; has also been listed as CTO & Chairman 2020-2022)
profile: Indian-born engineer who founded Reltio in 2011 (with Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva) after leading MDM product strategy at Siperian and Informatica. Reltio sells a cloud master-data-management / 'data unification' platform, valued around $1.7-2B, and now pitches it as the data foundation for enterprise AI.
interesting_fact: Before enterprise software, Sood was educated as a mechanical engineer (Andhra University, graduated 1995) in India.
deep_cut_fact: He told interviewer Adam Mendler that he began his career working on the automation of large-scale power plants, a natural hook for an energy/data-center podcast.

public_contacts.value: reltio@allisonpr.com (Allison + Partners, media and analyst inquiries)

notes: Press contacts per Reltio press releases (Kevin Keenan, VP Communications, listed in 2026 release); verify current contact on latest release. Frequent podcast guest (Modern CTO, DataVersity).

name: Wade Crang
current_role: Co-founder, impact.com (listed as Co-Founder & Growth Technologist / VP Strategic Operations)
profile: Cal Poly graduate and ad-tech data specialist who co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008 with Todd Crawford, Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud and Lisa Riolo. The partnership-automation platform reached a ~$1.5-2B valuation; Crang remains with the company in a strategic/technology role.
interesting_fact: impact.com was founded by a group of former Commission Junction (CJ) affiliate-marketing veterans; Crang had been CJ's VP of Business Intelligence & Product.
deep_cut_fact: Before impact.com he was on the founding team at LeadPoint, where he built the business-intelligence architecture credited with lifting revenue per lead.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal accounts verified. Best route is via impact.com communications (contact block on latest press release; EMEA releases have listed impact@mww.com agency address).

name: Harry Kalodner
profile: Princeton computer-science PhD researcher who co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Steven Goldfeder to commercialise their Arbitrum research. Arbitrum became the most widely used Ethereum layer-2 rollup; Kalodner leads Offchain's engineering and technical vision.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic project: the three founders developed the technology at Princeton and published it as a 2018 paper before forming the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student he was lead author of BlockSci, an open-source blockchain analysis platform (2017 paper 'BlockSci: Design and applications of a blockchain analysis platform').
notes: Technical founder; appears on crypto podcasts (e.g. Masters of Web3).

name: Sten Saar
profile: Estonian entrepreneur who moved to London, worked in operations at onefinestay and Deliveroo, and in 2016 co-founded Zego with Harry Franks and Stuart Kelly to sell flexible insurance to gig-economy delivery drivers. Zego hit a $1B+ valuation in 2021, expanded into fleet and telematics car insurance, and reported monthly profitability in Q4 2024.
interesting_fact: Zego was born from a gap Saar spotted at Deliveroo: couriers had no flexible, pay-as-you-work insurance.
deep_cut_fact: At 17 in Estonia he launched a business selling notepads to students that earned about $1 million across four countries while he studied business and management.
notes: Has appeared on The F in Tech podcast. No generic press email confirmed; Zego newsroom pages list an obfuscated contact address.

name: Wes Schroll
profile: Massachusetts native who came to UW-Madison for its entrepreneurship programs and left to build Fetch Rewards with Tyler Kennedy, launching in 2013. The receipt-scanning rewards app grew to tens of millions of users and a ~$2.5B valuation; he still runs the Madison-based company.
interesting_fact: He came to UW-Madison in 2011 'mostly because I was attracted to the entrepreneurship programs' and left to build Fetch; UW later gave him its 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: Fetch's first version (2014) was an in-store scan-as-you-shop app that auto-applied coupons, test-run at Fresh Madison Market in Madison before pivoting to receipt scanning.
notes: Received UW-Madison 2023 Chancellor's Entrepreneurial Achievement Award. He has told CNBC the business spent six weeks on the edge of collapse early on.

name: Sri Nathan
current_role: Co-founder, Plume Design (listed variously as Head of Business Development / VP Major Accounts)
profile: Networking-industry executive credited, with Fahri Diner, Adam Hotchkiss and Aman Singla, as a co-founder of Palo Alto-based Plume Design (founded 2014), the cloud-managed home Wi-Fi/smart-home platform sold through internet service providers and valued around $2-3B. Earlier he was president & CEO of Jasmine Networks and held roles at Menara Networks and other networking firms.
interesting_fact: Plume sells its 'pods' and cloud Wi-Fi software mainly through ISPs (e.g. Comcast, Charter) rather than directly to consumers.
notes: Very little public information; identity and current title based only on insider-data aggregators and job-board listings. Holds a doctorate from UT Austin and undergraduate degree from University of Madras per MarketScreener (unverified elsewhere). Route via Plume corporate comms.

name: Ivan Dimov
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2016-May 2025), Orca Bio
profile: Engineer-turned-biotech founder (PhD applied biophysics, Dublin City University; postdocs at UC Berkeley and in Irv Weissman's Stanford lab) who co-founded Orca Bio in 2016 with Nate Fernhoff and Jeroen Bekaert. Orca develops high-precision allogeneic cell therapies (lead product Orca-T for blood cancers); Fernhoff succeeded him as CEO in May 2025 ahead of the BLA filing.
interesting_fact: He also co-founded Lucira Health, spun out of his Berkeley microfluidics work, which won FDA authorization for the first at-home COVID-19 self-test and was later acquired by Pfizer.
deep_cut_fact: His background is in electronics and bio-MEMS; he has said working with Stanford physicians changed his approach from 'building technology first' to starting from a clearly defined medical problem.
notes: CEO transition reported May 2025 (https://trial.medpath.com/news/902ccabbc6efd8da/orca-bio-appoints-co-founder-nate-fernhoff-as-ceo-ahead-of-2025-bla-submission-for-orca-t); his current exact title not confirmed. Also earlier co-founded Blobcode Technologies.

name: Sebastien Fabre
current_role: CEO, ReSee (Paris luxury resale marketplace), since Dec 2023
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Vestiaire Collective (2009), the Paris-based marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury fashion, and was its CEO/chairman for nearly a decade until Max Bittner took over in January 2019. Vestiaire later reached a $1.7B+ valuation; Fabre, a former ReSee board member, became ReSee's CEO in late 2023 to drive international expansion.
interesting_fact: He has stayed in second-hand luxury for 15 years: after building Vestiaire Collective he took over ReSee, a curated vintage luxury marketplace, in its 10th-anniversary year.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming ReSee's CEO he sat on its board, and he joined to work alongside its founders Sofia Bernardin and Sabrina Marshall.
notes: Appeared on French podcast 'En Orbite' (#21) about building Vestiaire: https://podcast.ausha.co/ovny-media/en-orbite-21-sebastien-fabre-vestiaire-collective-batir-une-licorne-qui-change-nos-usages

name: Yoni Assia
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, eToro Group (Nasdaq: ETOR)
profile: Israeli fintech founder who in 2007 co-founded eToro (originally RetailFX) in Tel Aviv with his brother Ronen Assia and David Ring. eToro pioneered social/copy trading, became an early crypto adopter, and listed on Nasdaq in 2025; it reports ~3.8M funded accounts and $18.5B in customer assets (end-2025).
interesting_fact: He received stock as a bar mitzvah gift and became a successful trader in high school, only to see those profits vanish when the dot-com bubble burst as he began military service.
deep_cut_fact: Per Cointelegraph's 'Crypto Stories' interview, a young programmer named Vitalik Buterin helped with the launch of crypto trading on eToro.
notes: Highly public and active on X. Named to Fortune 40 Under 40 (2020). Father David Assia co-founded Magic Software. No generic press/IR email confirmed; use eToro Media Center / IR site.

name: Jonas Karklys
current_role: Co-founder, Nord Security; CEO of NordPass (as of 2024)
profile: Lithuanian entrepreneur (BA business administration, Vilnius University) who co-founded Nord Security, maker of NordVPN, NordPass, NordLayer and NordLocker, with Tomas Okmanas and Eimantas Sabaliauskas. The bootstrapped Vilnius company reached a ~$3B valuation in 2023; Karklys runs the NordPass password-manager business.
interesting_fact: Nord Security was bootstrapped for years before taking outside capital and reached a $3B+ valuation, making it one of Lithuania's best-known tech unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: Before university he was an accomplished race car driver and ran Infosport, a Lithuanian sports news site; after university he co-founded 50Garage and invested in F-1.LT before Nord Security.
notes: Lower profile than co-founder Tomas Okmanas; has done Swisspreneur podcast (ep. 407, 2024).

name: Julio Cotorruelo
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Domestika (current status not fully confirmed)
profile: Spanish entrepreneur (Universidad de Deusto) who co-founded Domestika, which began in Spain as an online community/forum for creatives and became a global online creative-courses platform; it reached a ~$1.3B valuation in its 2022 Series D. He has been based in Palo Alto, California.
interesting_fact: Domestika started in the early 2000s as a Spanish-language forum for designers with no courses, and only later pivoted into the online-course platform with millions of students.
notes: Could not verify current role after web-search budget ran out; insider-data sites suggest he may no longer be active as CEO. Reported earlier venture Webactiva (2001, digital services for Spanish SMBs) is unverified. Co-founders include Tomy Pelluz, Gabriel Suchowolski, David Duprez; Daniel Villegas is COO.
